title: Advanced Functions — Mission 1: The Signal Decoder
description: A garbled broadcast is hitting the campus radio tower. The waveform hides a polynomial signature, and only function transformations can decode it in time.

leo.name: Leo Marsh
leo.description: Has memorized every transformation rule but forgets his own coffee.

oscilloscope.name: Oscilloscope
oscilloscope.description: Shows the live waveform as a graph.

signal_log.name: Signal Log
signal_log.description: A printout of the garbled function's key points.

elements.text: The signal's just a shifted, stretched version of a base function. If we identify the transformation, we can cancel it out.
Can't we just crank the volume until it sounds normal?

elements.prompt: Leo raises an eyebrow at you.

options.text: "Let's pull the signal log and compare it to the parent function's graph first."
"Just start turning knobs until it looks right."

elements.text: Good, you're reading the log instead of guessing. Let's break the transformation down piece by piece.
Knob-turning got us nowhere. We need to actually name the transformation.

config.question: The signal matches g(x) = f(x - 3) + 2, where f(x) = x^2. What happened to the parent graph?

options.text: Shifted 3 units right and 2 units up
Shifted 3 units left and 2 units down
Reflected over the x-axis and stretched
Compressed horizontally by a factor of 3

config.explanation: f(x - h) + k shifts the graph h units right and k units up when h and k are positive.

config.prompt: Order these transformations of f(x) from most subtle to most dramatic change in shape.
Ren: "If f(x) = 2x + 6, what's f inverse of x? Type it like (x-1)/2."

elements.text: Signal's clean. We reversed the transformation and the broadcast is back.
It's working, barely. Next time, name the transformation before you touch anything.

elements.prompt: The tower hums back to life. What now?

options.text: Show Ren how to read any transformed graph from its equation.
Log off. The signal's clean, that's the win for today.

elements.text: So every weird graph is really just a plain one that got shifted, stretched, or flipped. That's oddly comforting.

ending.title: Signal Decoder Hero
ending.description: Restored the broadcast and taught the team to read any transformed function.

ending.title: Broadcast Restored
ending.description: The signal's clean. The deeper lesson can wait until tomorrow.
